title: Life Cycles of Animals
seo_title: Primary 3 Science: Life Cycles of Animals Worksheets (with Answers)
standard_code: Primary 3: Cycles in plants and animals (Life cycles of animals)
standard_text: Show an understanding that different animals have different life cycles: some have three stages (egg, nymph, adult) and some have four stages (egg, larva, pupa, adult); frogs and chickens also go through stages as they grow. Observe that young animals may or may not resemble their parents (summary of the MOE Primary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Primary 3 science worksheets for Singapore pupils on life cycles of animals: butterfly, mosquito, beetle, cockroach, grasshopper, frog and chicken, larva, pupa and nymph. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Animals grow through stages to become adults.
key_sub: Egg, larva, pupa, adult; or egg, nymph, adult.
body_html:
How to think about it

A life cycle is the stages an animal goes through as it grows into an adult that can reproduce.

  • Four stages: egg → larva → pupa → adult (butterfly, mosquito, beetle). The larva looks very different from the adult.
  • Three stages: egg → nymph → adult (cockroach, grasshopper). The nymph looks like a small adult without wings.
  • Frog: egg → tadpole → young frog → adult frog. Chicken: egg → chick → adult.
Example

Which stage comes after the larva in a mosquito's life cycle?

Egg → larva → pupa → adult

The pupa comes next

Answer: The pupa.

Example

Why should we not leave water in pails at home?

Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water

Larvae grow there

Answer: To stop mosquitoes from breeding.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a cockroach has a pupa stage. It has egg, nymph and adult only.
  • Thinking a caterpillar is a different kind of animal. It is the larva of a butterfly.
  • Thinking a tadpole is a fish. It is a young frog.
  • Thinking the pupa eats a lot. It does not eat while it changes.

faq.q: What is the difference between a larva and a nymph?
faq.a: A larva looks very different from the adult and later becomes a pupa. A nymph looks like a small adult without wings and has no pupa stage.

faq.q: Which animals have a four-stage life cycle?
faq.a: The butterfly, mosquito and mealworm beetle: egg, larva, pupa and adult.

faq.q: Why do we remove stagnant water in Singapore?
faq.a: Mosquitoes lay eggs in still water. Removing it stops the larvae from growing into adults, which helps to prevent dengue.

items.q: In the life cycle of a chicken, which stage comes after the egg?
items.e: The life cycle of a chicken is: egg → chick → adult chicken.

items.q: How many stages are there in the life cycle of a cockroach?
items.e: Cockroach: egg → nymph → adult cockroach.

items.q: How many stages are there in the life cycle of a mealworm beetle?
items.e: Mealworm beetle: egg → larva (mealworm) → pupa → adult beetle.

items.q: In the life cycle of a chicken, which stage comes after the chick?

items.q: Which of these animals has a tadpole stage in its life cycle?

items.q: Which of these animals has a nymph stage in its life cycle?

items.q: Which animal has a four-stage life cycle?
items.e: Egg → larva → pupa → adult.

items.q: Does a pupa eat?
c: Yes, it eats more than the larva.
No. It does not eat or move much while it changes.
items.e: The pupa uses food stored by the larva.

items.q: What is a young cockroach called?
items.e: A nymph looks like a small adult without wings.

items.q: Which of these animals has a nymph stage in its life cycle?

items.q: What is the stage of a butterfly between the caterpillar and the adult?
items.e: Inside the pupa, the caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

items.q: How many stages are there in the life cycle of a grasshopper?

items.q: In the life cycle of a frog, which stage comes just before the tadpole?
items.e: The life cycle of a frog is: egg → tadpole → young frog → adult frog.

items.q: In the life cycle of a cockroach, which stage comes just before the nymph?
items.e: The life cycle of a cockroach is: egg → nymph → adult cockroach.

items.q: What is a young frog that lives in water called?
items.e: Tadpoles have tails and gills.

items.q: In the life cycle of a frog, which stage comes after the young frog?
items.e: The life cycle of a frog is: egg → tadpole → young frog → adult frog.

items.q: What is a life cycle?
c: the stages an animal goes through from egg or birth to adult
items.e: The adult then reproduces and the cycle starts again.

items.q: Which animal has a three-stage life cycle?
items.e: Egg → nymph → adult.

items.q: Which stage comes first in the life cycle of most animals?
items.e: Many animals start life as an egg.

items.q: How many stages are there in the life cycle of a mosquito?
items.e: Mosquito: egg → larva → pupa → adult mosquito.

items.q: A chick hatches from an egg. What does it grow into?
items.e: Chick → adult chicken.

items.q: What happens to a tadpole as it grows into a frog?
c: It grows legs and loses its tail.
items.e: It also starts to breathe through lungs.

items.q: Why does a nymph shed its skin (moult) several times?
c: Its hard outer skin does not grow, so it sheds it to grow bigger.
It is turning into a pupa.
items.e: Cockroach and grasshopper nymphs moult as they grow.

items.q: Does the young (larva) of a mosquito look like its parent?
c: Yes, it is a smaller copy of the adult.
No, it looks very different from the adult.
Yes, but it has more legs.
items.e: The young changes a lot as it grows: egg → larva → pupa → adult mosquito.

items.q: How is a caterpillar different from an adult butterfly?
c: It has no wings and eats leaves.
items.e: The caterpillar changes completely inside the pupa.

items.q: Which statement about a frog's life cycle is correct?
c: Frogs give birth to young frogs.
Tadpoles live in water; adult frogs can live on land and in water.
Adult frogs breathe only through gills.
items.e: Frogs are amphibians.

items.q: In the life cycle of a butterfly, which stage comes after the caterpillar (larva)?
items.e: The life cycle of a butterfly is: egg → caterpillar (larva) → pupa → adult butterfly.

items.q: Which stage of a mosquito can fly?
items.e: Only adult mosquitoes have wings.

items.q: Where does a hen keep her eggs warm?
c: in a nest, by sitting on them
items.e: The heat helps the chicks develop.

items.q: Does the young (chick) of a chicken look like its parent?
c: Yes, it looks like a smaller adult.
Only after it becomes a pupa.
items.e: The chick looks like the adult but is smaller.

items.q: Which young animal looks most like its parent?
items.e: Nymphs are small copies of the adult.

items.q: Does the young (larva) of a mealworm beetle look like its parent?
c: Yes, it is a smaller copy of the adult.
No, it looks very different from the adult.
Yes, but it has more legs.
items.e: The young changes a lot as it grows: egg → larva (mealworm) → pupa → adult beetle.

items.q: How is a nymph different from an adult grasshopper?
c: It is smaller and has no fully grown wings.
items.e: A nymph looks like a small adult.

items.q: Where does a butterfly usually lay its eggs?
c: on the leaves of the plant its caterpillars eat
items.e: The caterpillars hatch on their food.

c: Only after it becomes a pupa.
Yes, it looks like a smaller adult.
items.e: The nymph looks like the adult but is smaller and has no wings.

items.q: Which shows the life cycle of a frog in the correct order?
c: egg → tadpole → young frog → adult frog
adult frog → young frog → tadpole → egg
egg → young frog → tadpole → adult frog
tadpole → egg → young frog → adult frog
items.e: Start with the egg and end with the adult.

items.q: Why do some animals lay many eggs?
c: Many eggs and young are eaten or die, so laying many helps some survive.
items.e: Frogs and fish lay hundreds of eggs.

items.q: Mealworms are fed to pet birds. Which stage of the beetle is a mealworm?
items.e: A mealworm is the larva of the mealworm beetle.

items.q: Why should we remove stagnant water from flower pot plates?
c: It makes the plants grow too fast.
Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water.
items.e: No still water means no place for mosquito larvae to grow.

items.q: A pupil changes the water in his vase every 3 days. A mosquito egg takes 2 days to hatch and the larva takes 7 days to become a pupa. Can adult mosquitoes come from the vase?
